memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports mild dyspnea on climbing two flights of stairs, otherwise independent in ADLs.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 4/5 (recall 3 items, clock draw normal), negative screen.
falls: no falls in last 12 months; gait steady; timed up-and-go 9 seconds, within normal range.
medicines: 2 regular (tiotropium inhaler OD, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD); salbutamol inhaler SOS as needed.
mood: denies low mood or anxiety; reports good sleep.
carers: husband, Rajesh, spouse.
goals: "I want to stay active at work and keep up with my daily walks."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
tiotropium inhaler 18 mcg inhalation OD
budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg inhalation BD
salbutamol inhaler 100 mcg inhalation SOS

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 1.68 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.90 L (88% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.58 (58%). Post-bronchodilator FEV1 1.80 L (59% predicted).

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: notes increased breathlessness on exertion, uses salbutamol 3-4 times/week; otherwise manages housework.
cognition: Mini-Cog not repeated (annual screen due next visit).
falls: no falls; gait slightly slower on heels; timed up-and-go 10 seconds.
medicines: 2 regular (tiotropium OD, budesonide-formoterol BD); salbutamol SOS usage up.
mood: reports occasional frustration with breathlessness; denies depression.
carers: husband, Rajesh, spouse.
goals: "I would like to reduce my inhaler use and feel less tired after work."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg inhalation BD increased to 2 puffs BD
tiotropium inhaler 18 mcg inhalation OD unchanged
salbutamol inhaler 100 mcg inhalation SOS

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Chest X-ray: lungs hyperinflated, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation or pleural effusion. Cardiac size within normal limits.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: "Over the past week I have felt more short of breath after walking to the bus stop, and I needed my rescue inhaler twice today. Is this normal?"

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Referred to Pulmonology, Apollo Specialist Centre, for evaluation of worsening COPD symptoms and possible need for escalation of therapy.

memories.author: D06
memories.text: Pulmonology advice: continue current bronchodilators, consider adding roflumilast 500 mcg OD if exacerbations persist; advise annual influenza vaccine and pneumococcal vaccination; repeat spirometry in 6 months.

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports better tolerance to walks after using roflumilast started per pulmonology advice; salbutamol use down to 1-2 times/week.
cognition: Mini-Cog score 3/5 (recall 2, clock draw mild abnormality), negative screen.
falls: no falls; gait normal; timed up-and-go 9 seconds.
medicines: 3 regular (tiotropium OD, budesonide-formoterol BD, roflumilast OD); salbutamol SOS as needed.
mood: feels more optimistic; denies anxiety.
carers: husband, Rajesh, spouse.
goals: "I want to keep working full‑time without needing frequent breaks for breathlessness."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
roflumilast 500 mcg oral OD
budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg inhalation BD
tiotropium inhaler 18 mcg inhalation OD
salbutamol inhaler 100 mcg inhalation SOS

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 1.75 L (57% predicted), FVC 2.95 L (90% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.59 (59%). SpO2 room air 94% (rest).

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
function: reports occasional mild dyspnea on hurried walking; able to complete workday without rescue inhaler.
cognition: Mini-Cog not due (annual screen next visit).
falls: no falls; gait steady; timed up-and-go 9 seconds.
medicines: 3 regular (tiotropium OD, budesonide-formoterol BD, roflumilast OD); salbutamol SOS minimal.
mood: stable; reports good energy.
carers: husband, Rajesh, spouse.
goals: "I aim to maintain my current activity level and avoid any exacerbations."

memories.author: D06
memories.text:
tiotropium inhaler 18 mcg inhalation OD
budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg inhalation BD
roflumilast 500 mcg oral OD
salbutamol inhaler 100 mcg inhalation SOS – advise to use only if wheeze develops.
